links.outcome: F1 of LLM approaches vs traditional LightGBM structured-data model on 30-day ED revisit prediction
links.effect: All LLM approaches (F1=0.3022-0.4505) failed to exceed LightGBM on structured data (F1=0.4614, 95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789]); benchmarking against simpler model showed no LLM advantage.
links.quote: Despite having access to comprehensive structured and unstructured clinical data, all LLM approaches (F1=0.3022-0.4505) failed to exceed a traditional LightGBM model using only structured data (F1=0.4614 (95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789]))).

links.outcome: Whether complex LLM approaches outperform simpler non-LLM model for the task
links.effect: Simple LightGBM on structured EHR features (F1=0.4614) exceeded all LLM-based methods (F1=0.3022-0.4505).
links.quote: However, we also found that a structured EHR baseline achieved performance (F1=0.4614 (95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789])) that exceeded LLM-based methods (F1=0.3022–0.4505).

links.outcome: Effect of retrieval augmentation with 10 similar cases on LLM direct prediction F1
links.effect: RAG improved all direct-prediction models, e.g., Claude 3.7 F1 from 0.3755 to 0.4160; GPT-4o from 0.3403 to 0.3867.
links.quote: The most significant gains were observed in GPT-4o (from F1=0.3403 to 0.3867) and Claude 3.7 (standard), with the latter achieving the highest overall F1 score of 0.4160 (95% CI [0.4024, 0.4294]) among direct prediction methods.

links.outcome: Precision-recall tradeoff of LLM predictions, over-prediction of high risk
links.effect: Deepseek R1 and Claude 3.7 (reasoning) favored high recall (>85%) at expense of precision (<20%), producing excessive false positives.
links.quote: The precision-recall breakdown reveals that models exhibited different operational characteristics, with Deepseek R1 and Claude 3.7 (reasoning) favoring high recall ( > 85%) at the expense of precision ( < 20%), while GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 (standard) achieved a more balanced precision-recall profile.

links.outcome: Absence of prospective evaluation of LLM predictions' clinical impact
links.effect: Study was retrospective and did not prospectively evaluate impact on clinical decision-making or patient outcomes; no external validation.
links.quote: We did not prospectively evaluate the impact of these predictions on clinical decision-making or patient outcomes.

links.outcome: External validation of models on data from other sites
links.effect: Chronological split with no patient overlap used, but external validation was precluded as no comparable public ED dataset exists.
links.quote: Our dataset includes EHR components unavailable in MIMIC-IV-ED, the only publicly available ED dataset, precluding external validation.

links.outcome: direct prediction F1 with retrieval augmentation
links.effect: Claude 3.7 F1 improved from 0.3755 to 0.4160 with retrieval augmentation.
links.quote: Retrieval augmentation improved direct prediction performance (e.g., Claude 3.7 F1 from 0.3755 (95% CI [0.3647, 0.3864]) to 0.4160 (95% CI [0.4024, 0.4294])), and embedding-based methods consistently outperformed direct approaches, with LLM2Vec achieving F1=0.4505 (95% CI [0.4345, 0.4666]).

links.effect: Zero-shot LLM F1 scores were 0.3022–0.3889, with high recall at the expense of precision.
links.quote: Direct zero-shot prediction using LLMs yielded modest performance (F1 scores 0.3022–0.3889), with these models demonstrating a tendency toward high recall at the expense of precision.
